name: The Design Matcher
oneLiner: Diffs Figma reference exports against live-app screenshots captured across desktop and phone viewports, and flags every screen that's missing, partial, or unreachable on mobile.
lead: Pairs each screen's Figma export with a Playwright-captured screenshot of the running app at every configured viewport, classifies each as MATCH / PARTIAL / NOT_IMPLEMENTED by counting which viewports actually produced a capture, and emits a side-by-side report. The key signal: a feature that renders on desktop but has no mobile capture surfaces as a PARTIAL (desktop-only) with a per-device reason.
chore: The manual path: open the app, resize to each phone viewport, navigate to every screen, screenshot it, open the matching Figma export, and eyeball the pair — across dozens of screens and multiple viewports. Slow, error-prone to track, and non-deterministic between reviewers.
instead: One command drives a headless browser through every screen at every viewport, captures each, pairs it with its Figma reference, and classifies the gap deterministically — same navigation, same viewports, same output every run.
whyItMatters: A feature that renders on desktop but is unreachable on mobile is a dead end for phone users. Counting captures per viewport catches that before it ships.

howItWorks.step: Drives the live app through every mapped screen at each viewport via `npx playwright test`, screenshotting each. A non-zero Playwright exit is downgraded to a warning, since screens not yet built on mobile legitimately fail to capture.
howItWorks.explain: Shells out to the capture spec with `execSync` and a **600s timeout** — a full sweep navigates every screen at every viewport, so the ceiling is generous. The `cd` into `browser/` matters: it anchors Playwright's config, deps, and output resolution to that root regardless of where the agent was launched. Passing `DESIGN_CAPTURE_SCREENS` only when `screenFilter` is non-empty lets a caller re-shoot a single screen without re-running the whole set. The critical decision is the empty `catch`: Playwright exits **non-zero if any capture fails**, but a screen not yet built on mobile *should* fail to capture, so the error is logged `warn` and swallowed — those screens become `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` downstream rather than crashing the run.

howItWorks.step: Resolves each screen's Figma reference PNG from the design source dir and copies it into the report working dir; missing exports are logged and skipped.
howItWorks.explain: Walks the static `FIGMA_SCREENS` map and, for each screen whose export **exists on disk**, copies it into the report working dir renamed from its Figma export name to `<screen.id>.png` — that rename is what lets `matchScreens` later pair reference to capture by **screen id** rather than by the designer's arbitrary filename. A screen whose export is **absent** is logged `warn` and simply never added to the returned `Map`, so downstream it renders a live capture with no reference beside it rather than throwing. The map is keyed by `screen.id`, the same key the capture filenames use, which keeps the join trivial.

howItWorks.step: Joins each screen to its Figma reference and probes the captures dir for a `<screenId>-<viewport>.png` at every viewport, recording captured true/false per viewport.
howItWorks.explain: For each screen it resolves the reference (falling back to `null` when the export was missing), then probes the captures dir for a `<screenId>-<viewport>.png` at **every** viewport — presence on disk is the entire signal, there is deliberately **no pixel diffing** here, only capture-existence per device. That is the key design choice: a screen that renders on desktop but produced no phone PNG shows up as `captured: false` on the mobile viewports, which is exactly what a desktop-only feature looks like. `status` is left as the stub `'NOT_CAPTURED'` and `observations` empty — `analyzeGaps` owns the actual classification, so this step stays a pure presence probe.

howItWorks.step: Classifies each screen by capture count: all viewports = MATCH, zero = NOT_IMPLEMENTED, desktop-only = PARTIAL with a per-device missing reason, anything else = PARTIAL.
howItWorks.explain: Deterministic classification from three tallies — total captured, whether **desktop** captured, and how many **mobile** viewports captured — with the branches checked **top-down and mutually exclusive**, so their order encodes precedence. `capturedCount === 0` wins first (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, unreachable in this build); then all-viewports (`MATCH`); then the branch this whole agent exists for — **desktop present but zero mobile** → `PARTIAL` flagged `DESKTOP-ONLY`, which calls `addPerDeviceMissingReasons` to attach a human reason per missing device (buried in a swipeable row, desktop-sidebar-only, no mobile entry point). Everything else is a mixed `PARTIAL` with a `captured/total` note. No LLM and no thresholds: the same capture set grades identically every run.

howItWorks.step: Aggregates the per-status counts (matching / partial / notImplemented / captured) and packages every screen's detail into one timestamped report object.
howItWorks.explain: Reduces the classified `ScreenComparison[]` into a single `ComparisonReport` — totals plus one count per status bucket. Note `captured` and `matching` are **not** the same metric: `captured` counts screens where **any** viewport landed a shot (`captures.some`), whereas `matching` counts only fully-`MATCH` screens, so a desktop-only `PARTIAL` still increments `captured` but not `matching`. The `timestamp` is emitted here so the JSON and its rendered `.md`/`.docx` siblings share one suffix and successive runs sit side by side rather than overwriting. `includeLandscape` is carried through so the renderer knows how many viewport columns to expect.

howItWorks.step: Renders the report to Markdown — summary counts, a per-screen status section, and a side-by-side image table (Figma | desktop | phone A | phone B) — plus an optional Word doc with the images embedded.
howItWorks.explain: Builds the report line-by-line into a string array joined on newlines. It leads with the headline counts — `matching`, `partial`, `notImplemented` relabeled **Full Responsive / Partial / Not Reachable** — the numbers a reviewer scans first, then per screen emits a `### label — status` heading, the side-by-side image table (Figma reference next to each viewport's capture), and every `observation` as a bullet, including the per-device missing reasons `analyzeGaps` attached. Because the observations were populated upstream, this renderer stays pure formatting — no re-classification here. With `--word` the same structure is emitted as a `.docx` with the PNGs embedded rather than linked.

examples.caption: Settings screen renders on desktop only
examples.input: Figma export of a Settings dialog, plus the live app to capture against.
examples.output: Classified `PARTIAL` (DESKTOP-ONLY): desktop capture present, no mobile capture at any phone viewport. Per-device reason: no Settings entry point in the mobile nav.

examples.caption: Card unreachable in a horizontal-scroll row
examples.input: Figma export for a 'Summaries' card sitting fourth in a swipeable card row.
examples.output: Classified `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on mobile — the capture navigation never scrolled to the card. Reason attached: buried in a horizontally-scrolling row.

examples.caption: Home screen matches at every viewport
examples.input: Figma export of the home screen, plus captures from desktop and three phone viewports.
examples.output: Classified `MATCH` — captured at all viewports, rendered as a side-by-side row showing the greeting, chat input, and menu button present on each.

underHood.heading: Capturing every screen at every viewport
underHood.whenRuns: First, unless invoked with `--report-only` to rebuild from existing captures.
underHood.input: The static screen map plus per-screen navigation.
underHood.output: Playwright screenshots at each viewport written to the local captures dir — no cloud device lab.

underHood.heading: Resolving Figma references
underHood.input: Exported Figma PNGs in the local design source dir.
underHood.output: Each reference copied into the report working dir, keyed by screen id for pairing.

underHood.heading: Pairing capture to reference per viewport
underHood.whenRuns: After both captures and references are resolved.
underHood.input: Every capture filename plus the copied reference map.
underHood.output: A per-screen match record listing which viewports produced a capture.

underHood.heading: Classifying the gap
underHood.output: A `MATCH` / `PARTIAL` / `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` label plus a per-device reason for each missing viewport (e.g. buried in a swipeable row, desktop-sidebar-only).

underHood.heading: Emitting the report
underHood.whenRuns: Last, after all screens are classified.
underHood.output: A JSON report and a Markdown report, plus — with `--word` — a `.docx` with reference and every viewport's capture embedded side by side.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
The target app running at a reachable URL (dev or QA) — the agent captures it live, not from a mockup.
A local dir of Figma-exported PNGs, one per mapped screen, filenames matching the screen ids.
~10-15 min on first run: `npx playwright install` downloads the Chromium and WebKit engines before any capture.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime for the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program executed by Node. One-time install per machine.
steps.firstRun: Only needed once per new machine.

steps.label: Install dependencies — once for the agent, once for the Playwright package it drives.
steps.cmd:
cd path/to/the-agents
npm install

cd Playwright
npm install
npx playwright install   # downloads the actual Chromium + WebKit browser engines
steps.why: The agent lives in the project root; the browser-driving layer lives in a sibling `Playwright` dir with its own deps. `npx playwright install` fetches the Chromium + WebKit engines — they aren't bundled with the npm package.
steps.firstRun: Downloads deps plus the browser engines — the slow part (5-10 min).
steps.rerun: No-op once installed, unless a dependency or browser version changed.

steps.label: Set the target URL and drop in the Figma exports.
steps.cmd:
export APP_URL=https://your-app-url/home

# copy the designer's exported PNGs into inputs/mobile/pages/,
# named to match each screen the agent knows about
steps.why: `APP_URL` is the live app the capture spec navigates; unset, it falls back to a built-in default that won't be your app. The PNGs are the reference half of each diff — a screen with no export renders its live capture with nothing to compare against.

steps.label: Run it.
steps.why: The full run: captures every mapped screen at every viewport (desktop + phones), pairs each with its Figma reference, classifies the gap, and writes the report. `--word` additionally emits a `.docx` with images embedded side by side.
steps.firstRun: Navigates and captures every screen at every viewport from scratch — the ~10 min part.
steps.rerun: `--report-only` rebuilds the report from on-disk captures without re-capturing; `--capture-only` does the inverse (refresh captures, skip the report).

steps.label: Open the generated report.
steps.why: The `.md` is the side-by-side diff — Figma reference next to the live capture at each viewport, each screen labeled `MATCH`, `PARTIAL`, or `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

inputs.name: APP_URL (environment variable)
inputs.desc: URL of the running app to capture.

inputs.name: inputs/mobile/pages/*.png
inputs.desc: Figma-exported reference PNGs, one per mapped screen, filenames matching screen ids.

inputs.name: --screens <list>, --landscape, --capture-only, --report-only, --word
inputs.desc: Flags to filter screens, add landscape viewports, split capture/report phases, or emit a `.docx`.

outputs.name: design-comparison-<timestamp>.json / .md
outputs.desc: Machine-readable and rendered report — per-screen status and observations.

outputs.name: design-comparison-<timestamp>.docx (optional)
outputs.desc: `.docx` with the Figma reference and every viewport's capture embedded side by side; emitted only with `--word`.

outputs.name: outputs/mobile/captures/*.png
outputs.desc: Raw captures, one per screen per viewport — reused by `--report-only` on a later run.

runbook.rerun: `--report-only` skips capture entirely and rebuilds the report from whatever is in the captures dir — useful when only the Figma references changed. A flagless run always re-captures, since there's no content-hash/fingerprint of the live app the way document-based agents fingerprint their inputs.
runbook.integrate: Wire the full run into a nightly or pre-release CI job so every merge gets a fresh diff. Treat any screen that flips MATCH → PARTIAL or NOT_IMPLEMENTED as a regression to triage before ship.

video.caption: 3-4 min screen recording: point the agent at the live app and the Figma exports, and watch the side-by-side diff report build.
script: Open a terminal next to the folder of the designer's exported screen pictures so viewers see both.
Say: 'This agent puts the designer's drawing next to the real app and shows you exactly where they differ — on desktop and on phones.'
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; say one line about what Node is.
Run `npm install` in the project root and in the Playwright folder (or note it's already done); mention `npx playwright install` downloads the actual browser engines it drives.
Show the one `export APP_URL=...` line; say 'this is the only place the live app's address lives.'
Show the folder of design PNGs; point out the filenames match the screen list the agent knows about.
Run `npm run design:compare -- --word`; narrate the log lines as it opens each device size and captures each screen.
Open the produced `.md` report; scroll to a full MATCH (side-by-side pictures lining up) and a PARTIAL (desktop-only) example.
Point out the plain-English reason under the partial one, e.g. 'buried in a swipeable row.'
Close: 'Run this before every release and a broken phone screen never quietly ships.'
